description: Phase 0 review fix (DECISIONS #review-0-r0 F1, Claude findings 1–2 and Sol finding 2, blocker): packages/core/src/sentences.ts `sliceInline` gives a zero-width atomic inline node (an image with empty alt, `![](x.png)`, alone or inside a link) no owner at the end of a paragraph and two owners at offset 0, so `replaceSentence` and `reorderSentences` silently delete or duplicate it; the mark branch's `hi <= lo` test discards zero-width descendants the same way. Decide the ownership rule for width-0 inline nodes at slice endpoints once (an explicit `includeAtTo` argument, true only for the final slice that reaches `plain.length`; drop the `zeroWidth && start === from` special case), traverse wrappers (link, emphasis, strong) that contain them, write the rule in the doc comment, and add the invariant the corpus never had: for every top-level paragraph of every fixture listed in fixtures/markdown/index.json, `format(reorderSentences(root, id, identity))` and `format(replaceSentence(root, id, i, <the sentence's own text>))` equal `format(root)` byte-for-byte. No new dependencies; no edits outside packages/core/src/sentences.ts and packages/core/test/.
acceptance: Probe cases from the reports pass as tests, each asserting node presence, count and URL, presence and absence: `One. Two. ![](i.png)` with replaceSentence(index 0, 'X.') → `X. Two. ![](i.png)` and reorderSentences(identity) unchanged; `![](i.png) One. Two.` with replaceSentence(index 0, 'X.') → exactly one image; `Hi. ![](x.png)` identity reorder unchanged; a linked empty-alt image `[![](x.png)](https://e.x)` at the end and at the start survives replace and reorder with its URL; an image adjacent to another image survives. The corpus-wide identity invariant passes for every paragraph of every fixture in index.json (count read from the index, not written as a literal). The 30 cases of sentences.cases.json and the existing sentences tests still pass; `pnpm lint && pnpm test && cargo test` green.

description: Phase 0 review fix (DECISIONS #review-0-r0 F2, Sol findings 3 and 5, blocker): packages/core/src/sidecar.ts's hand-written front-matter scalar scanner treats malformed scalars as writable (`title: bad: mapping`, `title: "\q"`) and misdecodes valid double-quoted escapes (`"\u0041"` mirrored as `u0041`, not `A`); a replacement value containing a newline is written literally inside single quotes as two physical lines and reported as success. Define the supported grammar for the two app-owned keys (PRD §6.1): plain scalar with no `: ` or ` #` sequence and no leading indicator character; double-quoted with the YAML escapes `\\ \" \n \t \r \/ \b \f \0 \uXXXX \xXX` decoded and re-encoded; single-quoted with `''`. Everything else (unknown escapes, malformed plain scalars, block or flow indicators, a replacement value containing `\n` or `\r` for any quoting style) → `FrontMatterUnsupported` before any edit, root identity and every byte unchanged. No YAML library (PRD §4; zero new dependencies); edits only in packages/core/src/sidecar.ts and packages/core/test/.
acceptance: Tests assert, for each case, both the outcome and the untouched bytes: `"\u0041"` reads as `A` and re-encodes preserving the quoting; `"\q"` and `bad: mapping` reads report FrontMatterUnsupported and a write leaves the block byte-identical; a multiline replacement (`Line one\nLine two`, and with `\r`) is refused for plain, single-quoted and double-quoted titles; the existing sidecar tests (73 at r0) still pass; `pnpm lint && pnpm test && cargo test` green.

description: Phase 0 review fix (DECISIONS #review-0-r1 G1, G2, G7 and G8; Sol finding 2 and Claude finding 1, blocker; Grok finding 1 and Claude finding 3, should-fix required): packages/core/src/sidecar.ts's front-matter writer still disagrees with its reader about what is representable. (a) Key identity: `KEY_LINE` compares literal key spellings, so a double- or single-quoted spelling of an app-owned key is neither a duplicate of the plain spelling nor found on its own; `writeFrontMatter` then rewrites the plain line beside the quoted duplicate (ok:true, the duplicate stays), or appends a second spelling. Rule: any quoted spelling of `title` or `question` in the block makes that key unsupported (FrontMatterUnsupported, root identity, every byte unchanged) whether it appears alone or beside the plain spelling; the block's other keys stay readable. (b) One quoting predicate: `needsQuoting` tests only tab, newline, `#`, `:` and the leading indicator, and the single-quoted branch of `serializeScalar` escapes only the apostrophe, so a replacement value containing U+0000, another C0 or C1 control, DEL, U+2028, U+2029 or a lone surrogate is written raw with ok:true; invariant A then fails on the written document, and `KEY_LINE` (a dot under the u flag without the s flag) classifies the block as malformed on the next read. Derive every quoting decision from one predicate that owns `encodeDoubleQuoted`'s escape table (plus U+2028, U+2029 and lone surrogates), route the single-quoted branch through it (promote to double-quoted rather than emit raw), and match key lines with an explicit character class instead of a dot. (c) The unchanged-value skip runs after the newline refusal, so a no-op write of a double-quoted value whose decoded form contains a newline (which the reader accepted and classified writable) is refused: run the `entry.value === value` skip first and refuse only a value that would actually be rewritten. (d) The rule promoted into CLAUDE.md names an unchanged front-matter value as a corpus-wide identity case and no test carries it. No YAML library, no new dependencies; edits only in packages/core/src/sidecar.ts and packages/core/test/.

description: Phase 1 follow-up required by task 1.10's phase check ("typing latency p95 with 10k words on /dev/editor: < 16 ms or a follow-up task is inserted at reconciliation"; DECISIONS #review-1-r0 F5 — Claude findings 2 and 7, Sol finding 5 required). Measurements at r0, all Linux headless Chromium, Vite dev build: rendered view p95 15.0 / 13.9 / 14.1 ms at 10k words and 26.3 ms at 20k (Claude: keydown → first mutation of the markdown pane, both timestamps in-page, 120 presses); 38.6 / 39.5 ms (Sol: beforeinput → the next timer task after input and observer work); source view p95 40.6 ms at 10k words (Claude, same harness as its rendered run). The two protocols differ by 2.5× on the same tree, so the number is protocol-bound; the cost is not: every rendered doc-changing transaction runs `pmToMdast` over the whole document (`packages/editor/src/store.ts:167`), the /dev/editor snapshot re-runs `format(root)` on every `useSyncExternalStore` read (`apps/desktop/src/dev/DevEditor.tsx:72`), and every source-view keystroke re-parses the whole buffer (`packages/editor/src/toggle.ts:479`; `parse` is 37 ms at 10k words against `format` 0.9 ms). Incremental `pmToMdast` is not built here: append the option with the r0 numbers to docs/V1.1-BACKLOG.md. Phase 1 review fix (DECISIONS #review-1-r2 H1 — Claude finding 1 blocker; H5 — Claude finding 5; H6 — Claude finding 6; the F1/G4 family in `stripUnparsableWhitespace`, packages/editor/src/schema.ts, a file of passed tasks 1.13 and 1.25, whose records are not edited): the strip's ownership rule stops at every atom and says nothing about an atom that is a block's **last** node, so a `hard_break` left at the end of a paragraph or heading reaches `format`, which writes it as a bare trailing `\` that `parse` reads back as a literal backslash — `format(parse("one\

description: Phase 1 review fix (DECISIONS #review-1-r2 H8 — Sol finding 2, filed against docs/V1.1-BACKLOG.md:44 and reconciled as a required should-fix: the r1 deferral of the ` ` family's emphasis-edge member rested on the claim that it is unreachable while Phase 1 binds no mark-toggle command, and the claim is false). description: Phase 1 review fix (DECISIONS #review-1-r2 H2 — Sol finding 1 blocker; the seam of passed tasks 1.17 and 1.24, whose records are not edited): a flush inside a continuous source typing burst splits undo history when the continuation outlasts one coalescing window. Reproduction (Sol, `/report/probe.mjs` and `probe.log`): blank /dev/editor, toggle to source, type `a`, click Copy Markdown, return the caret to the source view, type `bcdef` at 300 ms per character, press Ctrl+Z at once → `a` remains (Ctrl+Shift+Z restores `abcdef`); the same burst without the Copy (`control.mjs`) undoes to empty. Sol's keystroke times: 242, 308, 612, 924, 1237, 1543 ms — every adjacent gap under 314 ms, the two commits' keystroke times 1,300 ms apart. Cause: `bindCodeMirror` (packages/editor/src/toggle.ts) keeps one time for the pending segment, `pendingAt`, its **latest** keystroke, and `push` (packages/core/src/undo.ts) decides continuity by one distance, `at - present.at` — the previous entry's last keystroke against the segment's last keystroke — so the adjacent keystrokes between them are invisible, and 1.24's grouping rule (the chain of keystrokes that becomes one commit is the chain that became one coalesced entry before 1.17) holds only for a segment shorter than the window; 1.24's case 3 stops its continuation at 200 ms and never reaches this. Fix: the pending segment carries both its first and its last keystroke time; continuity is decided between the segment's **first** keystroke and the previous entry's last, and the entry keeps the **last** for the next comparison. Thread it through the contract rather than around it: `PushOptions` (core) gains `from` — the earliest keystroke of the batch, defaulting to `at` — and `push` merges when `from` is within the window of the present entry's `at` (a clock that went backwards still starts a new step); the store's `commit` passes it through; the binding records the first keystroke time when a segment opens and the latest on every `change`, and its commit carries both; the rendered view and every other caller are unchanged (`from` defaults to `at`). Restate the grouping rule in the module comment (it is stated once; make it true again: continuity is a property of adjacent keystrokes, so a segment is continuous with the previous entry when its first keystroke is, however long the segment runs). Explicit closure on a toggle and on a history command (`endCoalescing`, `beforeHistory`) is preserved. Tests with the injected clock (`now` and `schedule` options), one per case, named in the journal: (a) a commit, then a continuation whose total duration exceeds the window while every adjacent gap is under it, ending by the timer — one undo entry; (b) the same continuation ending by a flush — one entry; (c) a continuation whose first keystroke lands more than a window after the previous commit — two entries, whether timed or flushed (the genuine-gap absence case); (d) the 1.24 cases unchanged and green; (e) a core test in packages/core/test for `from`: presence (merges when `from` is inside the window and `at` is outside) and absence (`from` omitted behaves as before). Playwright in e2e/web/editor-toggle.spec.ts (the 1.24 reproductions are the model): Sol's reproduction as real chords with `delay: 300` — after Ctrl+Z the pane and the surface are empty; after Ctrl+Shift+Z they read `abcdef\n`. G9's revisit trigger fires here (DECISIONS #review-1-r1 G9: the first task that changes `bindCodeMirror`'s commit path after 1.24): add the third reported line to e2e/web/latency.spec.ts's source-view measurement — `commit: p50/p95, n=<bursts>`, the deferred whole-buffer `parse` at the burst boundary — evidence only, no threshold, reported the way the existing two lines are. Scope: packages/core/src/undo.ts, packages/core/test/**, packages/editor/src/store.ts, packages/editor/src/toggle.ts, packages/editor/test/**, e2e/web/**, docs/lessons.md, the journal. Principal reading, to be confirmed from that log and the spec before anything changes, never assumed: the case places the caret with `page.keyboard.press("ControlOrMeta+Home")` — Meta+Home on macOS — and three `ArrowRight`. The assertion meant to catch that, `expect(page.locator(".ProseMirror em")).toHaveText("b ")`, cannot: `toHaveText` normalises whitespace, so `b` satisfies it; and the pane assertion `a *b* c` is the same bytes whether the space was typed inside the mark (moved out by the clause) or outside it after the delimiter, so on no runner did the case prove that the keystroke built Sol's tree. Never a `Home` or `End` key and never a `ControlOrMeta+` chord in the rendered view; state the rule once in the file's doc comment in words. The absence case's `ControlOrMeta+End` (spec line 101) is the same construct and is replaced the same way — it passed on macOS only because the seed's click had already left the caret at the end. (2) Every assertion on the ``'s text is byte-exact: `textContent()` compared with `toBe("b ")` in the H8 case (the space went inside the mark; the document keeps it there and the clause runs on the way out) and `toBe("b")` in the absence case, and, for the input-rule case that by its title accepts either tree, an explicit regex naming both (`/^word ?$/` after the space, `toBe("word")` after the `x`) — never `toHaveText`, which normalises whitespace and is the assertion that let the miss through.
